title: Day 47 · Week 6, Day 5 — Protocol: the kitchen rules — one bacterium, one metal, one parasite, the fish list that says eat more, and the thermometer that settles most of it
summary: The third Protocol episode, for the father who took over the kitchen on Day 37. Your baby is 5–7 mm at the turn to Carnegie stage 15, lens vesicles closing, nasal pits, hand plates, and a gut that is a straight tube feeding on nothing — so only what crosses her blood matters. One bacterium justifies the list: Listeria, ~1,250 US cases and 172 deaths a year, about 1 pregnant woman in 25,000, 1 in 4 of them losing the pregnancy or newborn (CDC); in the French MONALISA cohort (818 cases, 107 maternal-neonatal) only 5% of pregnancies were uneventful, 24% ended in fetal loss, and no loss occurred after 29 weeks or more than 2 days after admission — early treatment works. The 2003 FDA/FSIS risk assessment by food: deli meats ~77 cases per billion servings and the majority of all cases, unreheated frankfurters 65, smoked seafood 6, soft unripened cheese 2, pasteurised milk 1, a reheated frankfurter 0.06; the 2011 cantaloupe outbreak (147 ill, 33 dead, 7 pregnancy-related, 1 miscarriage) and the 2024 deli-slicer outbreak (61 hospitalised, 10 dead). The CDC and NHS swap lists, and the size: roughly one in a million sandwiches, fixed by 165 °F. One metal justifies a short list: the FDA/EPA advice is 8–12 oz of fish a week, 2–3 servings, with seven species to avoid, and the FDA table shows why — swordfish 0.995 ppm, shark 0.979, bigeye 0.689, albacore 0.35, light tuna 0.126, salmon 0.022, scallops 0.003; ALSPAC's 11,875 mothers (Hibbeln 2007): no seafood, verbal-IQ bottom quartile OR 1.48. One parasite justifies a thermometer: Toxoplasma, 91% of US women susceptible (NHANES), transmission 6% at 13 weeks to 72% at 36 (Dunn 1999, 603 infections), 30–63% of infections from undercooked or cured meat and cats not a risk factor (Cook 2000); rare lamb aOR 8.4, raw ground beef 6.7, local cured meat 2.0 (Jones 2009); 2 congenital cases in 521,655 Californian births. USDA temperatures (145/160/165 °F), the ordinary bugs that don't cross (eggs, sprouts, raw juice, 40 °F, two hours), the three-agency sushi argument, the cross-references (liver, game, caffeine, alcohol), the fever-plus-aches rule, and the six-line fridge card.
action: Tonight, three objects and one card. Buy a fridge thermometer and a probe thermometer tomorrow if they aren't in the house; tonight check the fridge is at or below 40 °F (4 °C). Move everything from the chilled ready-to-eat shelf — deli meat, hot dogs, soft cheese without 'pasteurised' on the label, smoked salmon, the tub of coleslaw, sprouts — to one shelf labelled 'heat or yours'. Write six lines on a card for the fridge door: ready-to-eat from the chiller gets heated to 165 °F; whole meat 145 °F and rest, ground 160, poultry 165; fish two to three times a week, not the seven big ones, tuna steak once; eggs firm or Lion; no sprouts, raw juice, raw milk or raw fish; fever plus aches is a call. Photograph the card for her phone.
